title: State Police Constable Entry Guide
summary: Prepare for state police constable recruitment with physical and written exam tips.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The State Police Constable Entry Guide offers candidates an incredible opportunity for a secure and prestigious career. It requires candidates to clear a multi-tier selection process that rigorously tests their aptitude, physical fitness, and overall capability. Thousands of aspirants apply every year, making it one of the most competitive career paths available today. Strategic preparation based on the latest examination syllabus is vital to stand out and succeed.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Parameter | Requirements |
|---|---|
| **Educational Qualification** | Must have passed 10th, 12th, or Graduation depending on the exact post profile from a recognized state or central board / university. |
| **Nationality** | Must be a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated with the intention of permanently settling. |
| **Stream/Subject** | Specific technical streams or Science/Maths/English requirements may apply for specialized and technical cadre roles. |
| **Minimum Percentage** | Typically 50% to 60% aggregate score is required in the qualifying examination, varying based on category and recruitment notification. |
| **Document Verification** | Valid ID proof, educational certificates, domicile, and category certificates must be produced in original at the final stages. |
| **Additional Diplomas** | Desirable for higher technical roles or specified non-technical positions. |
| **Computer Literacy** | Basic knowledge of computer operations is often expected and sometimes certified. |

## Age Limit & Relaxation

| Category | Base Age Limit | Age Relaxation Years |
|---|---|---|
| **General (UR)** | 18 - 25/27/30 Years (Varies by specific notification) | None (0 Years) |
| **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** | 18 - 25/27/30 Years | Up to 3 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Scheduled Castes (SC)** | 18 - 25/27/30 Years | Up to 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** | 18 - 25/27/30 Years | Up to 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)** | 18 - 25/27/30 Years | Up to 10 Years upper age relaxation (General), 13 (OBC), 15 (SC/ST) |
| **Ex-Servicemen (ESM)** | As per standard guidelines | Typically 3 years after deduction of military service rendered |
| **Departmental Candidates** | As per standard guidelines | Up to 40/45 years of age based on years of continuous service |

## Physical Standards & Test

| Parameter | Male Standard | Female Standard |
|---|---|---|
| **Minimum Height** | 157 cm - 170 cm (Varies widely by region and post) | 152 cm - 157 cm (Varies widely by region and post) |
| **Chest (Unexpanded)** | Minimum 77 cm to 80 cm | Not Applicable |
| **Chest Expansion** | Minimum 5 cm expansion required | Not Applicable |
| **Weight** | Proportionate to height and age as per medical standards | Proportionate to height and age as per medical standards |
| **Running (Sprint)** | 1.6 km run in 6.5 to 7 minutes | 800 meters run in 4 to 5 minutes |
| **Long Jump** | 11 to 14 feet in up to 3 chances | 9 to 10 feet in up to 3 chances |
| **High Jump** | 3.5 to 4 feet in up to 3 chances | 3 feet in up to 3 chances |
| **Vision / Eye Sight** | Minimum 6/6 or 6/9 without glasses, no color blindness | Minimum 6/6 or 6/9 without glasses, no color blindness |

## Written Exam Pattern

| Subject / Section | Total Questions | Maximum Marks | Duration / Time Allowed | Negative Marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 25 to 50 Questions | 50 to 100 Marks | Combined with other sections | 0.25 / 0.50 per incorrect answer |
| **General Awareness / Current Affairs** | 25 to 50 Questions | 50 to 100 Marks | Combined with other sections | 0.25 / 0.50 per incorrect answer |
| **Quantitative Aptitude / Mathematics** | 25 to 50 Questions | 50 to 100 Marks | Combined with other sections | 0.25 / 0.50 per incorrect answer |
| **English Comprehension / Language** | 25 to 50 Questions | 50 to 100 Marks | Combined with other sections | 0.25 / 0.50 per incorrect answer |
| **Domain Specific Subject**| 50 to 100 Questions| 100 to 200 Marks | Separate timings may apply | 0.25 / 0.50 per incorrect answer |
| **Overall Grand Total** | **100 to 250 Questions**| **200 to 500 Marks**| **60 to 180 Minutes** | **Applicable uniformly** |

## Preparation Strategy Overview

| Preparation Phase | Recommended Action Plan for Candidates |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Foundation Building** | Understand the complete syllabus thoroughly. Collect standard reference books, study materials, and begin clearing fundamental concepts across all subjects. |
| **Phase 2: Intensive Practice** | Solve previous year question papers. Enroll in structured mock test series. Analyze performance metrics, identify weak areas, and allocate extra time to improve them. |
| **Phase 3: Final Revision** | Create short, crisp notes for quick recall. Focus on current affairs of the last six months. Avoid picking up completely new topics just before the exam. |
| **Phase 4: Physical & Mental Health**| Maintain a balanced diet, ensure adequate sleep, and incorporate daily physical exercises to clear medical and physical efficiency tests effortlessly. |
